settings.title: A 30-second weekly check-in
settings.text: Once a week, rate your energy, recovery, stress and sleep out of 10. Felt changes are easy to forget, so writing them down turns a feeling into a record you can look back on.

settings.title: HRV
settings.text: The number that reacts to everything: busy weeks, workouts, short nights. Read it as a 30-day average against your own baseline, never a single morning. If your device shows a stress score, track it alongside.

settings.title: Resting heart rate
settings.sub: Slow to move, easy to read
settings.text: Creeping up usually means your week is outrunning your recovery. Compare the 30-day average at day 30 and day 90 with your starting point.

settings.title: Sleep
settings.text: Duration, consistency and your sleep score, as your device records them. Note late nights, travel and alcohol so you can read around them.

settings.title: Readiness or Body Battery
settings.text: WHOOP Recovery, Oura Readiness, Garmin Body Battery and others. Read the trend, next to how the day actually felt.

settings.name: Nicotinamide riboside
settings.text: A direct NAD+ precursor: your cells convert it in two steps. 300mg is the dose the published human work is built on, not a fraction of it.

settings.name: Trimethylglycine
settings.text: A methyl donor. NAD+ metabolism uses methyl groups up, so TMG puts them back rather than leaving the rest of the pathway competing for them.

settings.name: Vitamin D3
settings.text: Most people in the UK run low between October and March. Included at a daily dose rather than a token one.

settings.name: Vitamin K2 (MK-7)
settings.text: Pairs with D3: K2 directs calcium towards bone rather than soft tissue. The MK-7 form stays in circulation longest.

settings.name: Methylated B complex
settings.text: Eight B vitamins, every dose declared: thiamin 5mg, riboflavin 5mg, niacin 16mg NE, pantothenic acid 10mg, B6 as P5P 5mg, folate 400µg, B12 100µg and biotin 300µg. Active forms throughout — B6 as P5P, folate and B12 methylated — because NAD+ metabolism spends methyl groups, and these are the forms that put them back without the liver having to convert them first.

settings.name: Zinc (bisglycinate)
settings.text: Chelated for absorption, and easier on an empty stomach than the oxide form.

settings.name: Copper (bisglycinate)
settings.text: Balances the zinc. A daily zinc dose without copper beside it depletes copper over time.

settings.name: Grapeseed extract
settings.text: Polyphenols, standardised rather than a whole-fruit powder, so the dose on the label means something.

settings.name: Trans-resveratrol
settings.text: The trans isomer specifically — the form the research uses, and the one that survives the shelf.

settings.name: Coenzyme Q10
settings.text: Carries electrons inside the mitochondria. Levels fall from your thirties onwards, and statins lower them further.

settings.name: PQQ
settings.text: Studied for its role in mitochondrial biogenesis: making new mitochondria rather than only running the ones you have.

settings.name: Bioperine®
settings.text: Black pepper extract. It is here because it improves the absorption of several of the ingredients above.

settings.title: How will I know if it’s working?
settings.text: Note your starting point before your first capsule: a 30-second check-in (energy, recovery, stress and sleep, each out of 10), or a 7-day average from your wearable. Then compare at day 30, 60 and 90. Single days are noise; months are signal.

settings.title: Do I need a wearable?
settings.text: No. The 30-second weekly check-in works on its own. If you do wear one (Garmin, WHOOP, Oura, Apple Watch and others), use the same device for the whole 90 days and compare 30-day averages of HRV, resting heart rate and sleep.

settings.title: Will it help with stress?
settings.text: It isn’t a calming supplement, and it won’t make a hard week easy. Vitamins B6, B12, thiamin, niacin and biotin contribute to normal psychological function, and pantothenic acid to normal mental performance. To see how busy weeks land, rate stress in your weekly check-in, or track HRV and your device’s stress score, and compare with your starting point.

settings.title: When might I notice something?
settings.text: Give it 60 to 90 days, taken daily, before you judge it. Some people notice a difference in their energy or recovery within the first few weeks; others notice nothing early on. Read wearable data as 30-day averages, not single nights. That’s why the guarantee runs for 90 days.

settings.title: Is it safe with my other supplements?
settings.text: In most cases, yes, and coffee is fine. Watch for doubling up: a separate B complex, zinc, vitamin D, K2 or NAD+ product will overlap with what’s already in MUTO, so check your other labels against ours. If you take prescription medicine, check with your GP or pharmacist first: MUTO contains vitamin K2 (100µg), which can affect blood thinners such as warfarin. Not for use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or for anyone under 18.

settings.title: What if it’s not for me?
settings.text:
If you subscribe, take MUTO daily and don’t see a difference within 90 days, we’ll refund every subscription payment you’ve made in that time, less our delivery costs. Email hello@mutolongevity.com within 14 days after your 90 days end with your name, order number and a line on your experience, and we’ll refund your original payment method within 7 working days. You don’t need to send any wearable data.

The guarantee covers first-time subscribers buying at muto.co, one claim per customer. One-time purchases and orders through Amazon or other retailers aren’t covered. You can skip, pause or cancel online at any time.

settings.title: Why not just take NR on its own?
settings.text: You can, but NR alone covers one input. MUTO pairs it with nutrients that have authorised roles in how your body makes and uses energy (B vitamins and copper for normal energy-yielding metabolism, zinc for protecting cells from oxidative stress), plus CoQ10, TMG, resveratrol and PQQ. One routine instead of several separate products.

settings.title: Is there caffeine in it?
settings.text: No. No caffeine and no stimulants, so there’s nothing to time around your day, and your coffee stays as it is. Every batch is third-party tested for identity, potency and contaminants before release.
